title: Handoffs, Viewboxes, Inter-script Air, Scopes & Springs
description: Transitions you can grab mid-flight, images that crop themselves, CJK/Latin auto-spacing, scoped anchor names and spring-morph controls.

drops.title: Transitions, Handed Over
drops.description: Safari 27 puts the live Animation object on transitionrun — so a running transition can be paused, reversed and scrubbed.
drops.concept: Until now, catching the animation behind a CSS transition meant calling getAnimations() and guessing which entry was yours. Safari 27 adds an .animation property to AnimationEvent and TransitionEvent that hands you the object directly. This demo captures every transition three cards fire, meters them live, and lets you pause, reverse, re-rate and scrub them mid-flight — with the getAnimations() lookup as the fallback path where the property has not shipped.

interaction.mouse: Click any card to fire its four transitions; drag the scrub slider to move all of them to the same point
interaction.click: Run all / Pause / Reverse / Finish drive every captured Animation at once
interaction.touch: Cards are tappable and the whole control strip is touch-sized

drops.title: Crop Without a Wrapper
drops.description: object-view-box gives a replaced element its own viewBox, so panning and zooming happen without an overflow:hidden parent.
drops.concept: Cropping on the web has always cost an extra element — a clipping box plus an oversized image dragged around inside it. object-view-box moves the crop onto the image itself with an inset() rectangle, which means the element never moves in the layout and the crop is an animatable property. The wide lens here is draggable and zoomable; the six tiles below each hold a different inset() and re-crop on hover, with a transform-based fallback for engines that lack it.
drops.source: LogRocket — A guide to CSS object-view-box

interaction.mouse: Drag the wide lens to pan the viewBox; hover a tile to zoom its crop
interaction.click: Shuffle re-rolls all six tile crops; the mode button swaps native property for the JS fallback
interaction.touch: The lens pans with one finger; tiles zoom on tap

drops.title: Air Between Scripts
drops.description: text-autospace asks the engine for the quarter-space between ideographs and Latin that CJK typesetters insert by hand.
drops.concept: Japanese or Chinese set flush against Latin words and numerals collides, because the two scripts were drawn on different bodies. text-autospace hands the spacing rule to the engine — ideograph-alpha for letters, ideograph-numeric for digits — and Safari 27 adds the insert keyword. The demo sets each paragraph against a no-autospace baseline and against a manual hair-space build produced by walking the string for script boundaries, so the intent is visible even where the property has not shipped.

interaction.mouse: Slide the gap and size controls to retune the manual spacing and the type size
interaction.click: Three tabs switch between the property, hand-inserted hair-spaces and no spacing at all
interaction.touch: Tabs and sliders sit above the samples on narrow screens

drops.title: Anchors That Know Their Card
drops.description: Six cards sharing one anchor name send all six tooltips to the last card — anchor-scope walls each name into its own subtree.
drops.concept: Anchor names are globally visible, so a repeated component that names its anchor --card leaks: every tooltip resolves to the last matching element in the DOM. anchor-scope fixes it, and the catch is where it goes — on the common ancestor of the anchor and the positioned element, not on the anchor itself. Flip the switch here and six tooltips pile onto card six; flip it back and each returns to its own card, with position-area and the offset still tunable.
drops.source: Schalk Neethling — CSS anchor positioning: scoping, implicit anchors and conditional hiding

interaction.mouse: Hover a card to raise its tooltip; the scope switch shows the pile-up and the fix
interaction.click: Toggle anchor-scope, change position-area, pin or unpin every tip at once
interaction.touch: Tap a card to pin its tooltip when the show-all switch is off

drops.title: Press, Squeeze, Morph
drops.description: Material 3 Expressive makes shape the press state — and a real spring, sampled into a generated linear() easing, carries it.
drops.concept: M3 Expressive replaced the flat pressed colour with geometry: a button's corners collapse under your finger, the selected segment of a connected group rounds out while its neighbours compress, and a FAB morphs into a bar rather than scaling into one. The motion underneath is a damped spring, which CSS can now run natively by sampling the spring into a linear() easing — the bounce slider regenerates that easing live and every control on the page picks it up.

interaction.mouse: Hold a button to watch its corners collapse; pick a segment to squeeze its neighbours
interaction.click: The FAB morphs into a bar and back; sliders retune bounce, duration and resting corner radius
interaction.touch: Every control is a real button with a pointer-driven state layer
